clue.text: Indian heard to confess to doubling up

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for the Indian is taken as it is said aloud, not as spelt

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada
to sing is slang for confessing to the police

explanation.surface: A Native American, overheard owning up, is bent double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means a Native American, the Cree; 'heard' gives the sound of CREE written as CREA. 'Doubling up' is laughing helplessly, which in British slang is creasing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Creasing up is British slang for laughing so hard that one folds over.

clue.text: A social gathering this morning for a drink

definitions.text: A social gathering this morning for a drink

parts.words: A social gathering this morning for a drink
parts.note: the clue reads like an invitation to a morning get-together, a familiar British fundraising event named after the hot beverage served there

explanation.surface: An invitation to a morning get-together for refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: A coffee morning is a British social event, often for charity; the drink it is named after is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee is the hot drink served at a morning social gathering named after it.

clue.text: Every military officer originally contributed without hesitation to the fee

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of each of the three words is taken
without here means outside, the word for contributed going round the hesitation

parts.note: lent, as in lent a hand, means gave or contributed
um is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: Each army officer chipped in promptly towards the payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: LENT surrounds UM, after EMO from the first letters of 'Every military officer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An emolument is a salary, fee or payment for work.

clue.text: Scotch starts her weight going up — brisk movement needed

parts.note: the start of the word Scotch, its opening two letters

indicators.note: going up in a down clue means the weight abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: oz, ounce, is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: A whisky makes a woman's weight rise, so she needs vigorous exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' is musical: a scherzo is a lively section of a symphony. 'going up' reverses OZ in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A scherzo is a lively, playful movement in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Sikes's girl friend in France

explanation.surface: A villain's girlfriend is across the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist; the second definition is a place to be found in France, the city in Lorraine.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens gives the burglar a lover who is murdered by him, and the same name belongs to a city in north-eastern France.

clue.text: Joint that mends itself

indicators.note: mends suggests putting the letters of itself back together in a new order

explanation.surface: A joint in the body that heals by itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mends' is the anagram signal applied to ITSELF. The stifle is a horse's knee-like joint in the hind leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The stifle is the joint in the hind leg of a horse or dog, equivalent to the human knee.

clue.text: Method of creating work — in a time of shortage of permanent staff?

parts.note: temporary workers, temps, are taken on when permanent staff are lacking
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Asks how work gets done in a period when there are few permanent employees.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: an era of temps. 'work' means a work of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempera is a painting technique using pigment bound in egg yolk.

clue.text: Failing to give offence

explanation.surface: A shortcoming that causes upset.
explanation.definitionFit: A fault is a shortcoming or weakness, and also a misdeed or wrong committed.

clue.text: Exquisite Oriental leather work

parts.note: E stands for east, the Orient

indicators.note: work suggests the letters of leather are worked into a new shape

explanation.surface: Fine Eastern craftsmanship in leather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' is the anagram signal: LEATHER becomes THEREAL, after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethereal means delicate and light, too refined for this world.

clue.text: Melody containing note of distress

indicators.note: containing means the word for melody holds the note within it

parts.note: a strain is a passage of music, a melody
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tune that carries a sad sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To straiten is to put into difficulty, especially of money, as in straitened circumstances.

clue.text: Improvident way to eat

parts.note: food goes straight from the fingers to the lips with nothing kept back, the image behind living with no savings, spending all one earns at once

explanation.surface: A careless, wasteful manner of having a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes living with no reserve, spending money as soon as it comes in.

clue.text: Household officer eager at first to ask about the regiment

indicators.note: at first says only the opening letter of the word eager is used
about means the word for asking goes round the regiment's letter

parts.note: to query is to ask a question
R is a standard abbreviation for regiment

explanation.surface: A royal official is keen to start asking questions about the regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is an officer of the royal household who attends a member of the royal family.

clue.text: He encourages a gambler

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: A man who urges a gambler on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He encourages' is the definition, a person who abets.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage or assist, usually in wrongdoing, so an abetter is one who eggs another on.

clue.text: Poet is reviewed in books he favours

indicators.note: in places the shuffled poet-is letters inside the abbreviation for books

parts.note: NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

indicators.note: reviewed suggests the words poet is are looked at again and recast in a new order

explanation.surface: A poet is critiqued in volumes he likes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reviewed' rearranges POET IS into EPOTIS, which goes inside NT (New Testament).
explanation.definitionFit: A nepotist shows favouritism to relatives, especially by giving them jobs.

clue.text: Green tarantula ends up in cage

indicators.note: in puts the turned spider's ends inside the word for imprisoning

parts.note: to immure is to shut up or confine, to cage

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the two letters are read from bottom to top
ends means the first and last letters of the word tarantula

explanation.surface: A spider is caught and locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of tarantula, TA, reversed by 'up' give AT, which goes inside IMMURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or not fully grown, lacking maturity.

clue.text: Some scent a love of the classics is returning

indicators.note: is returning signals that the Latin word for love is read backwards

parts.note: amor is Latin for love, Latin being the language of the classics

explanation.surface: A fondness for ancient literature comes back with a certain whiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the classics' points to Latin: AMOR, love, read backwards with 'is returning' gives ROMA, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroma is a pleasant smell, a kind of scent.

clue.text: Away from the mountains, many went further

parts.note: out means away, as in out of the house
a range is a line of mountains
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred, many

explanation.surface: Leaving the high country, lots travelled on.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrange is to exceed in range, so something that outranged others reached beyond them.

clue.text: Refusing to agree to be put out, bowled, no score, by the Navy

parts.note: to stub a cigarette is to put it out
B is the cricket scoring abbreviation for bowled
O, zero, is no score
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: A cricketer won't accept being out, bowled for nought by a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is cricket, England's bat-and-ball game: a batsman bowled out for nought, a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Stubborn means obstinate, unwilling to yield.

clue.text: Instructor's exclamation of impatience to soldiers

parts.note: tut is the sound made to show irritation or disapproval
OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A teacher tuts impatiently at the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher who gives instruction.

clue.text: Recoup and insure again

explanation.surface: Win back losses and renew the policy.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain what was lost, and re-cover means to take out cover, or insurance, once more.

clue.text: Part of Asia is in this state — less than half

definitions.text: Part of Asia is in this state

explanation.surface: Some of Asia is in a particular condition, a lesser share.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: Asia MINOR is part of Asia, and the suffix -ITY means a state or condition, so Asia Minor appears in the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia Minor followed by the condition suffix, and a minority is the smaller number, under fifty per cent.

clue.text: Fiddles making a lot of noise

definitions.meaning: singular din, while the answer is plural; the plural of the noun means noisy scenes

explanation.surface: Violins producing a din.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddles' looks musical but means swindles.
explanation.definitionFit: Rackets are fraudulent schemes or swindles, and a racket is also a loud din.

clue.text: Makes one of several old coins

explanation.surface: Combines a few antique pieces of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The unite was an English gold coin of James I's reign.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together into a single whole, and unites were English gold coins of the early 1600s.

clue.text: Panda in bizarre cabaret

indicators.note: bizarre suggests the letters of cabaret are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A panda performs in an odd nightclub show.
explanation.definitionFit: The red panda is also called the bearcat.

clue.text: Expert in a small specialised sphere of activity

parts.note: dept is the shortened form of department, a specialised area of work

explanation.surface: A specialist in a narrow field.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept is someone highly skilled, a master of a craft.

clue.text: A slice of bread with lunch ain't free!

indicators.note: a slice of means a run of letters is cut from within the words lunch ain't

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that the bread served at lunch costs money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A slice of bread' hints at a sandwich, but 'A slice of' marks the letters taken from 'lunch ain't'; 'bread with' only dresses the surface. It echoes 'there ain't no such thing as a free lunch'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unchain is to set loose from fetters, to free.

clue.text: Show in America, belonging to a lady

parts.note: US is the United States of America
her is the possessive for a woman

explanation.surface: A display in the United States, owned by a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Show in' looks like 'exhibit in' but is a verb phrase: to escort someone in.
explanation.definitionFit: An usher leads guests to their places, so to usher is to escort someone inside.

clue.text: Misguidedly revetting with two hoes — clearly one too many

indicators.note: misguidedly suggests the letters are led astray into a new order
two asks for the garden tool to be counted twice

parts.note: a hoe is a garden tool; the plural says more than one is wanted

explanation.surface: Someone building a retaining wall with a pair of garden tools has plainly had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with two hoes' supplies HOE twice (HOEHOE) to go with REVETTING; 'Misguidedly' rearranges the lot. Revetting is facing an embankment with masonry.
explanation.definitionFit: Having had one drink beyond the limit is a British idiom for being slightly drunk.

clue.text: Kind of sunburn seen around the river

indicators.note: around signals the word for sunburn is turned back to front

parts.note: a tan is the bronzing of skin by the sun
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A sort of sunburn is visible all around the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns TAN into NAT; the Ure, a Yorkshire river, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature means kind or sort, as in things of that nature.

clue.text: Campaigns, these days, get involved in many stratagems

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many

indicators.note: get involved in places the abbreviation for these days inside the word for tricks

parts.note: ruses are crafty stratagems or tricks
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Modern campaigns become entangled in a lot of tactical schemes.
explanation.definitionFit: Crusades are vigorous campaigns for a cause, originally the medieval holy wars.
